why: First turn with the baseline fitted as the training-time device it is (ADR 0048). baselineR2 read 0.07054 on five consecutive runs while the lambda moved all over, and every lambda below 1.0 takes its advantage as V(next) - V(here), so that number was capping the whole mechanism. Two things were wrong with it and both are measured on this exact dataset. The alpha was shared with the action rows, which are fitted on sixty examples each and want the small number, while the baseline wanted a far larger one: held-out r2 0.0705 at 10 against 0.1021 at 10000. And the fit predicted returns that cannot happen -- from -1.78 to +2.19 where Returns.Of bounds everything to 1.05 -- which in rounds 15 and beyond made it worse than predicting a constant, r2 -0.2179 against -0.0014. Clipping and a separate alpha together take it to 0.1053 overall and from -0.2179 to +0.0685 in the late game, which is exactly where the high-lambda policies live: ci-81 played 19.1 rounds against Greedy and capped 46.2% of matches. Watch the win rate against Greedy and against search-4, not r2 and not baselineR2. Note baselineR2 is not comparable with the five runs before this: it is now measured on the values actually used, and the step change on identical data is 0.0705 to 0.0806. Nothing here has been played yet -- this is a fit that is less wrong, not an agent that is better, and the lambda sweep found the value policy topping out near 0.10 against Greedy where the clone plays 0.725. Open: the nonlinear baseline ADR 0048 leaves on the table (0.1215 by gradient boosting, and the engine never reads it), and whether the features are the real ceiling.
